papers.title: Alloy Selection and Manufacturing Technologies for Total Ankle Arthroplasty: A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) has evolved significantly through advances in alloy selection and manufacturing technologies. This narrative review examines the metallurgical foundations of contemporary TAA implants, analyzing primary alloy systems and their mechanical properties. Cobalt-chromium alloys provide superior mechanical strength and durability but present metal ion release concerns, while titanium alloys (Ti6Al4V) optimize biocompatibility with elastic modulus values (101-113 GPa) closer to bone, despite tribological limitations. Novel β-titanium formulations (Ti-35Nb-7Zr-5Ta, Ti10Mo6Zr4Sn3Nb) eliminate toxic aluminum and vanadium components while achieving lower elastic modulus values (50-85 GPa) that better match cortical bone properties. Manufacturing has transitioned from traditional methods (investment casting, forging, CNC machining) toward additive manufacturing technologies. Selective laser melting and electron beam melting enable patient-specific geometries, controlled porosity, and optimized microstructures, though challenges remain with residual stresses, surface finish requirements, and post-processing needs. Emerging biodegradable materials, composite structures, and hybrid implant designs represent promising future directions for addressing current material limitations. This review provides evidence-based insights for alloy selection and manufacturing approaches, emphasizing the critical role of materials engineering in TAA implant performance and clinical outcomes.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文综述了踝关节置换术的合金选择和制造技术，未涉及Ti-6Al-4V增材制造的后处理对疲劳性能的影响。
llm.why_not_core: The paper is a narrative review on total ankle arthroplasty implant materials and manufacturing, not a study on post-processing of AM Ti-6Al-4V for fatigue/mechanical performance; it does not provide experimental data or modeling on any post-processing treatment.

summary_en.motivation: To review the metallurgical foundations and manufacturing technologies for total ankle arthroplasty implants.
summary_en.method: A narrative review of primary alloy systems (Co-Cr, Ti6Al4V, β-Ti) and manufacturing methods (traditional vs. additive).
summary_en.result: Titanium alloys offer biocompatibility benefits but suffer from tribological limitations; additive manufacturing enables patient-specific designs but requires post-processing.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; this is a review article.

papers.title: A surface integrity-informed crystal-plasticity based modelling of fatigue crack initiation in aerospace-grade Ti-6Al-4V
papers.abstract: A Crystal Plasticity Finite Element Method (CPFEM)-based approach is developed to predict fatigue crack initiation sites in aerospace-grade Ti-6Al-4V in an as-machined condition. The model integrates an Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD)-reconstructed microstructure, incorporating prior deformation history, residual stress, and milling-induced roughness. The constitutive formulation employs Armstrong-Frederick kinematics with microstructure-sensitive fatigue indicators. Results show that fatigue initiation is highly localised, driven by surface topology, strain accumulation, and crystallographic variations with depth. Basal and prismatic slip systems dominate deformation, with Extreme Value Statistics (EVS) revealing their susceptibility to fatigue crack initiation. The findings highlight that Schmid factor alone does not fully explain fatigue hotspots, as local stress states, grain interactions, and surface-induced geometric constraints also play a critical role in crack initiation.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的后处理，而是针对传统制造方式的疲劳裂纹预测，因此与用户方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not address additive manufacturing (AM) Ti-6Al-4V; it studies conventionally manufactured aerospace-grade Ti-6Al-4V. No post-processing treatment relevant to AM (e.g., heat treatment, HIP, surface treatments) is investigated; the only processing considered is machining, which is not framed as a post-processing control for AM.

summary_en.motivation: To predict fatigue crack initiation in aerospace-grade Ti-6Al-4V by incorporating surface integrity from machining.
summary_en.method: A CPFEM approach integrating EBSD-reconstructed microstructure, deformation history, residual stress, and milling-induced roughness.
summary_en.result: Fatigue initiation is highly localized and driven by surface topology and strain accumulation, with Schmid factor insufficient to explain hotspots.
summary_en.validation: No explicit experimental validation; relies on Extreme Value Statistics from simulation results.
